title: Access keys, SAS tokens and stored access policies
learningObjective: Choose between account keys, account SAS, service SAS, user delegation SAS and Entra ID; create and revoke SAS safely with stored access policies; and rotate or disable keys without outages.
foundation: Every storage account has two access keys. Whoever holds a key has full control of all data in the account, so keys should be kept secret and rotated.
A shared access signature (SAS) is a URL token that grants limited access: chosen permissions (read, write…), on chosen resources, until an expiry time.

A stored access policy is a named rule saved on a container (or share, queue, table). A SAS that points to it inherits its permissions and expiry, and you can cancel all those SAS tokens at once by deleting or changing the policy.
The most secure option is to use Microsoft Entra ID with RBAC data roles, or a user delegation SAS that is signed with Entra credentials instead of a key.
engineer: Account keys (key1, key2): regenerating a key immediately invalidates the key and every account SAS and service SAS signed with it. Rotate safely: switch apps to key2, regenerate key1, switch back, regenerate key2. Store keys in Key Vault, set a key expiration policy, and monitor with Azure Policy or Advisor.

allowSharedKeyAccess = false blocks Shared Key and every key-signed SAS (account and service). Entra ID and user delegation SAS keep working. Check that tools such as the portal, AzCopy and apps use Entra ID before disabling it.

SAS types: account SAS (one or more services, service-level operations), service SAS (one service; can reference a stored access policy), and user delegation SAS (Blob/Data Lake only; signed with a user delegation key obtained with Entra credentials; valid at most 7 days; needs generateUserDelegationKey permission, for example Storage Blob Delegator).

SAS parameters: sv (version), ss/srt (account SAS services and resource types), sp (permissions), st/se (start and expiry), sip (allowed IPs), spr (https only), si (stored access policy), sig (signature). Validation fails with 403 when the signature, time window, IP, protocol or permissions do not match.

Stored access policies: up to five per container, share, queue or table. A SAS referencing a policy can omit permissions and expiry. Deleting or renaming the policy revokes every SAS that uses it; changes can take up to 30 seconds to apply. Ad hoc SAS (no policy) can only be revoked by rotating the signing key, or for a user delegation SAS by revoking the user delegation keys.
Best practice: short expiry, least privilege, HTTPS only, sip where possible, a SAS expiration policy on the account, and Entra ID instead of keys whenever the client supports it.

example.title: Revocable partner downloads
body: A partner needs read and list access to the reports container for a month. The admin creates a stored access policy 'partner-read' (rl, 30 days) and issues a service SAS that references it.

When the contract ends early, deleting the policy revokes the partner's SAS within seconds, without rotating keys and breaking every other client. Internal apps already use managed identities with Storage Blob Data Reader, so Shared Key is disabled later.

prerequisites: For user delegation SAS: an Entra identity with generateUserDelegationKey and a data role
permissions: Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listkeys/action to read keys (Storage Account Key Operator Service Role, Contributor)
Storage Blob Delegator (or a data role) for user delegation SAS
limits: Five stored access policies per container/share/queue/table
User delegation SAS: at most 7 days
Policy changes take up to 30 seconds
portal: Storage account > Security + networking > Access keys: show, copy or Rotate key; Set rotation reminder.
Storage account > Shared access signature: build an account SAS (services, resource types, permissions, IPs, protocol, expiry, signing key).
Container > Shared access tokens: build a service SAS or user delegation SAS (Signing method: Account key / User delegation key), optionally choosing a stored access policy.
Container > Access policy: add stored access policies (identifier, permissions, start, expiry).
Storage account > Configuration: Allow storage account key access = Disabled.
configuration.cli:
az storage account keys list -g rg-data -n stcontoso -o table
az storage account keys renew -g rg-data -n stcontoso --key key1
az storage account update -g rg-data -n stcontoso --key-exp-days 90
az storage container policy create --account-name stcontoso --container-name reports \
  --name partner-read --permissions rl --expiry 2027-01-01T00:00Z --auth-mode key
az storage container generate-sas --account-name stcontoso --name reports --policy-name partner-read --auth-mode key -o tsv
# User delegation SAS (no key):
az storage container generate-sas --account-name stcontoso --name reports --permissions rl \
  --expiry 2026-11-25T00:00Z --https-only --auth-mode login --as-user -o tsv
az storage account update -g rg-data -n stcontoso --allow-shared-key-access false
configuration.powershell:
New-AzStorageAccountKey -ResourceGroupName rg-data -Name stcontoso -KeyName key1
$ctxKey = (Get-AzStorageAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-data -Name stcontoso).Context
New-AzStorageContainerStoredAccessPolicy -Container reports -Policy partner-read -Permission rl -ExpiryTime (Get-Date).AddDays(30) -Context $ctxKey
New-AzStorageContainerSASToken -Name reports -Policy partner-read -Context $ctxKey
Remove-AzStorageContainerStoredAccessPolicy -Container reports -Policy partner-read -Context $ctxKey
$ctxEntra = New-AzStorageContext -StorageAccountName stcontoso -UseConnectedAccount
New-AzStorageContainerSASToken -Name reports -Permission rl -ExpiryTime (Get-Date).AddDays(1) -Context $ctxEntra
Set-AzStorageAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-data -Name stcontoso -AllowSharedKeyAccess $false

lab.objective: Issue, use and revoke SAS tokens, and see the effect of key rotation and disabling Shared Key.
steps: Set public network access to all networks. Generate a service SAS with read only and try a write.
Generate a SAS signed with key1, read successfully, then Rotate key1 and read again.
Generate a SAS that uses the stored access policy, read, then delete the policy and read again.
Untick 'Allow storage account key access'. Try the account key, then a user delegation SAS.
expected: Rotation breaks SAS signed with that key
Deleting the policy revokes its SAS
User delegation SAS still works without Shared Key

validation.text: A SAS was denied for a missing permission
Deleting a stored access policy revoked a SAS
Disabled Shared Key and saw key-based access rejected

failureScenarios: Long-lived ad hoc SAS with no way to revoke except rotation
Rotating the only key an app uses
Disabling Shared Key while tools still use keys

troubleshooting.symptom: 403 'Signature did not match' for a previously working SAS.
troubleshooting.cause: The signing key was rotated, or the URL was altered.
troubleshooting.fix: Issue a new SAS with the current key, or use a stored access policy / user delegation SAS.

troubleshooting.symptom: 403 'This request is not authorized to perform this operation using this permission'.
troubleshooting.cause: sp does not include the operation (for example list).
troubleshooting.fix: Generate a SAS with the needed permission letter.

troubleshooting.symptom: SAS works on Wi-Fi but not on mobile data.
troubleshooting.cause: sip restricts the SAS to specific IPs.
troubleshooting.fix: Widen or remove the IP restriction.

troubleshooting.symptom: Portal 'Switch to access key' fails after disabling Shared Key.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Microsoft Entra authentication with a data role.

comparisons.difference: Comparable to SAS, but signed with IAM credentials (closer to a user delegation SAS) and with no stored access policy equivalent.
No secrets to leak; access is per identity and auditable; preferred over keys and SAS.

misconceptions.reality: A SAS is just a URL; revoke it by deleting its stored access policy or rotating the signing key.

misconceptions.myth: An account SAS can use a stored access policy.
misconceptions.reality: Only a service SAS can reference a stored access policy.

misconceptions.myth: Disabling Shared Key breaks all SAS tokens.

architectureDecisions: Default to Entra ID with managed identities; use user delegation SAS for delegated access.
If you must use service SAS, always attach a stored access policy so it can be revoked.
Automate key rotation with Key Vault and alternate key1/key2.

learn: SAS settings: permissions, expiry, IP, protocol
Prefer Entra ID and user delegation SAS

steps.label: Master key
steps.title: Someone wants just one file
body: A partner needs to read one report. Giving them the account key would give them full control of every file in the account, forever.

steps.label: Keys
steps.title: Two access keys, so you can rotate
body: Every account has key1 and key2. Each gives full access. Rotate them regularly: move apps to key2, regenerate key1, and so on.
You can switch off key access completely (Allow storage account key access = Disabled) and use Microsoft Entra ID instead.

callout.text: Store keys in Azure Key Vault, never in code.

steps.label: SAS
steps.title: A SAS is a signed, limited link
body: A shared access signature (SAS) is a token added to a URL. It says what is allowed (read, write, list...), on what, until when, and optionally from which IP and over HTTPS only.
Account SAS and service SAS are signed with an account key. A user delegation SAS is signed with Microsoft Entra credentials and works for blobs only; it is the most secure.

steps.label: Revoke
steps.title: Stored access policies let you take it back
body: A SAS cannot be cancelled by itself; it works until it expires or the key that signed it is regenerated. A stored access policy on a container holds the permissions and expiry; a service SAS that refers to it can be revoked by changing or deleting the policy.
Up to five stored access policies per container.

callout.text: Regenerating a key breaks every SAS signed with it.

steps.label: Best
steps.title: The safest option
body: Use Microsoft Entra ID and RBAC for your own apps. When you must share a link, use a user delegation SAS with a short expiry.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Keys and SAS
body: Limited, expiring links beat master keys.
recap: key1 + key2 allow rotation without downtime
Account, service and user delegation SAS
Set permissions, expiry, IP and HTTPS
Revoke via stored access policy or key regeneration
Prefer Entra ID and user delegation SAS

handsOn.title: Share a file with a SAS link, then revoke it
handsOn.cost: Cents. A few small files in a Standard LRS account cost almost nothing; delete the account at the end.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.
A storage account in rg-az104-lab: Standard performance, LRS redundancy, default settings. Name it st<yourinitials><number> (lowercase letters and numbers only, globally unique).

steps.do: Create a container named reports and upload a small text file.
steps.see: The file in the container. Its access level is Private.

steps.do: Open the file > Overview and copy its URL into a new private browser tab.
steps.see: An error: the resource is not public.

steps.do: Back on the file select Generate SAS. Permissions: Read, expiry: 1 hour from now. Generate SAS token and URL. Copy the Blob SAS URL into the private tab.
steps.see: The file's contents in the browser.

steps.do: Open the reports container > Settings > Access policy > + Add policy. Identifier: read1h, permissions: Read, expiry: tomorrow. OK, then Save.
steps.see: read1h listed under Stored access policies.

steps.do: Open the container > Settings > Shared access tokens. Choose Stored access policy: read1h, Generate SAS token and URL. Add /<your file name> after the container name in the URL, before the '?', and open it.
Delete the read1h policy and Save. Wait 30 seconds and reload the policy-based link.
steps.see: An authentication error: the SAS was revoked. The first SAS still works until it expires.

steps.do: Open Security + networking > Access keys > Rotate key for key1 and confirm. Reload the first SAS link.
steps.see: It fails too: it was signed with key1.
steps.tip: Real apps using key1 would also break. Move them to key2 before rotating key1.

check: A SAS link worked, and you revoked one by deleting the stored access policy.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
